title: Victor Bertrandius witnesses Brown's gravitator experiments
summary: Jesse Michels tells of Victor Bertrandius witnesses Brown's gravitator experiments, about 1952 at Los Angeles, California, and frames it as the host. As told, not a fact.

tellings.quote: A lieutenant colonel from Wright Airfield who went on to become a general named Victor Bertrandius witnessed Brown's gravitator experiments in Los Angeles in 1952. He was quoted as saying, "Believe it or not, I think I just saw a flying saucer and it frightened me."

Bertrandias paid an unannounced visit to a demo of Brown's gravitator at the Towns and Brown Foundation in 1952. After witnessing the demo, he said, "Believe it or not, I saw a model of a flying saucer.
tellings.difference: Places it at the Townsend Brown Foundation as an unannounced visit, and quotes 'I saw a model of a flying saucer' with no mention of fear.
tellings.link_reason: Same 1952 witnessing of Brown's gravitator demo by Victor Bertrandias, with the flying-saucer quote.

as_told.title: Victor Bertrandias: 'I think I just saw a flying saucer'

plain: A podcast host, Jesse Michels, citing a biography of the inventor Thomas Townsend Brown by Paul Schatzkin, says that in 1952 in Los Angeles a lieutenant colonel from Wright airfield, an Air Force base, named Victor Bertrandias watched Brown's "gravitator" experiments, devices meant to move without ordinary propulsion. Bertrandias, who later became a general, is quoted as saying, "Believe it or not, I think I just saw a flying saucer and it frightened me." The story is told as a hint that humans may have been working on antigravity flight back then.
